**Exercise 1. Forecasting with ARMA(1,1) and Parametric Bootstrap**

• Write a function simulate_arma11 that takes as inputs starting values for Y (Y0), ε (eps0), the length of the series N, and parameters phi, theta, sigma, and returns a simulated series from an ARMA(1,1) process of length N. (Note that we use T instead of N in the lecture, but in R, T is reserved for TRUE.

```{r}

#rm(list = ls())   

simulate_arma11 <- function(Y0,eps0,N,phi,theta,sigma) {
  
  # Initialize vectors
  Y <- numeric(N)      # empty container for the series
  eps <- numeric(N)
  
  # Generate innovations from N(0, sigma^2)
  eps <- rnorm(n = N, mean = 0, sd = sigma) 
  
  # Simulate ARMA(1,1) process
  for (t in 1:N){
    
    if (t ==1) {
      Y[t] = phi * Y0 + eps[t] + theta * eps0
      
    } else {
       Y[t] <- phi * Y[t-1] + eps[t] + theta * eps[t-1]
    }
  }
  
  return(list(Y = Y, eps = eps))
  
}


```

• Use this function to generate a time series of length N = 200 from an ARMA(1,1) process with
starting values Y0 = 0 and ε0 = 0 and parameters ϕ = 0.6, θ = 0.3, and innovation variance
σ2 = 1.

```{r}
phi = 0.6
theta = 0.3
sigma = 1
N = 200

y <- simulate_arma11(0,0,200,0.6,0.3,1)$Y
# or y <- arima.sim(n = N, list(ar = phi, ma = theta), sd = sigma)

length(y)
plot(y, type = 'l')


```

• Split the data into a training set (70%) and a test set (30%).

```{r}

p_train <- 0.7
n_train <- floor(p_train * N)          # 70% of N
train   <- y[1:n_train]
test    <- y[(n_train+1):length(y)]
h <- length(test)  # test horizon

length(train)
length(test)
length(test) + length(train)



```

Fit an ARMA(1,1) model on the training data.

```{r}

fit <- arima(x = train, order = c(1, 0, 1), include.mean = FALSE)

coef(fit)       # ar1 and ma1, compare with 0.6 and 0.3
fit$sigma2      # variance, compare with 1

```

• Use the simulate_arma11 function to generate forecasts (what are the starting values in this case?):
– Simulate B = 500 bootstrap sample paths from the fitted model for the test horizon.
– From these bootstrap forecasts, compute the mean forecast and the 90% prediction interval (5% and 95% quantiles).

```{r}


B <- 500 # number of bootstrap paths
boot_preds <- matrix(NA, nrow = h, ncol = B)

# Generate paths
for(b in 1:B){
  
  boot_preds[,b] <- simulate_arma11(Y0=train[n_train], eps0=fit$residuals[n_train], N=h, phi=fit$coef["ar1"], theta=fit$coef["ma1"], sigma=sqrt(fit$sigma2))$Y
}

pred_mean <- apply(boot_preds, 1, mean)
alpha <- .1
pred_q_upper <- apply(boot_preds, 1, function(x) quantile(x, probs = 1- alpha/2))
pred_q_lower <- apply(boot_preds, 1, function(x) quantile(x, probs = alpha/2))



```


• Plot the results: training data, test data, bootstrap paths, mean forecast, and prediction interval.

```{r}

plot(y, type="l", col="white", main="Bootstrap Forecasts with 90% Prediction Band",
     ylab="y", xlab="t", ylim=c(-5,5))
lines(y[1:n_train])
# plot bootstrap paths
for(b in 1:B){
  lines(n_train + 1:h, boot_preds[,b], col=rgb(0,0,0,alpha=0.05))
}

# quantile forecast band
lines(n_train + 1:h, pred_q_upper, col="red", lwd=2, lty=2)
lines(n_train + 1:h, pred_q_lower, col="red", lwd=2, lty=2)

# shaded area for prediction band
polygon(c(n_train + 1:h, rev(n_train + 1:h)),
        c(pred_q_upper, rev(pred_q_lower)),
        col=rgb(1,0,0,alpha=0.2), border=NA)

# mean forecast
lines(n_train + 1:h, pred_mean, col="blue", lwd=2) # the forecast (from train data)
#lines(n_train + 1:h, test, col = 'white', lwd=2) # the truth (from test data)

legend("topleft",
       legend=c("Observed","Mean forecast","90% Prediction Band"),
       col=c("black","blue","red"), lty=c(1,1,2), lwd=c(1,2,2), bty="n")

```

• Evaluate forecast accuracy:
– Compute the RMSE of the mean forecast and of the upper quantile forecast.

```{r}

rmse_mean <- sqrt(mean((test - pred_mean)^2))
rmse_q_upper <- sqrt(mean((test - pred_q_upper)^2))
```

– Compute the quantile score for the mean forecast and for the upper quantile forecast.

```{r}

# quantile score on predicted quantile
mean_qs_upper <- mean(
  (1-alpha/2 - 1)*(test - pred_q_upper)*(test < pred_q_upper) +
    (1-alpha/2)*(test - pred_q_upper)*(test >= pred_q_upper)
)

# quantile score on mean
mean_qs_mean <- mean(
  (0.5 - 1)*(test - pred_mean)*(test < pred_mean) +
    (0.5)*(test - pred_mean)*(test >= pred_mean)
)

```

- Report the obtained scores.

```{r}

# print results
cat(paste0("RMSE on mean forecast: ", round(rmse_mean,4), "\n"))
cat(paste0("Mean Quantile Score on mean forecast: ", round(mean_qs_mean,4), "\n"))

cat(paste0("RMSE on 95% quantile forecast: ", round(rmse_q_upper,4), "\n"))
cat(paste0("Mean Quantile Score on 95% quantile forecast: ", round(mean_qs_upper,4), "\n"))

```
